lines.text: This is the two times table… and it's about to draw a heart.
Put some dots around a circle… and number them.
Now connect each number to its double. One goes to two… two goes to four… three goes to six.
And when you go past the last number, just keep counting from the beginning.
That's the whole rule. Now let's do it with four hundred dots instead of twenty… Watch.
There it is.
Look closely… there isn't a single curved line here. Every line is perfectly straight.
Nobody drew this heart. It just appears… in the edge where all those lines cross.
Now try the three times table… and the heart splits in two.
The four times table gives you three points… and five gives you four.
Can you see where this is going?
The number of points is always the multiplier… minus one.
Seven gives you six. Thirteen gives you twelve. No exceptions.
And if you raise the multiplier just a little at a time… the shapes melt into each other, forever.
But this isn't just a pretty picture. That heart has a name… it's called a cardioid.
It's the exact path a point traces on a coin… as it rolls around another coin of the same size.
And you've probably seen it at home.
When light from a faraway lamp hits a cup of coffee, the reflection draws the three times table… a shape called a nephroid.
Move the light right up to the edge of the cup… and the two times table comes back. The heart.
Take a look at your coffee tomorrow morning… and tell me in the comments if you can see it.
